canonical_hypotheses.accommodation_relevance: Provides individualized evidence about useful mobility and observed burden when evaluating inline skates as a non-traditional mobility aid.
canonical_hypotheses.background: Walking and controlled skating are repeated N-of-1 mobility states whose useful output and measured burden must be compared without treating wearables as pain instruments.
exclusion_rules: Exclude broad athletic or long-route skating from the controlled comparison unless separately labeled.
Do not substitute WHOOP overnight recovery HRV for Kubios/Polar H10 session HRV.
Do not infer a missing metric, cohort, session, distance, or pain value.
inclusion_rules: Use reviewer-accepted walking, Mall skating, and controlled PT skating observations.
Require compatible metric definitions, units, and session/window scope for each comparison.
Retain source labels, cohort mapping provenance, sample counts, and quality state.
interpretation_rules: Lead with measured cohort and paired-date findings.
Interpret FSI and CSS only after compatible primary metrics and coverage are visible.
Keep functional output, duration, distance, and unequal exposure beside burden comparisons.
limitations: This is repeated N-of-1 evidence from the current corpus, not a population estimate.
Wearables estimate burden dimensions and do not directly measure pain.
Controlled Mall skating, PT skating, and walking remain distinct mobility states.
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_question: How do walking and controlled inline skating differ in observed physiologic, movement, and functional mobility burden?
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_relevance: Tests whether controlled skating and walking occupy distinguishable multimetric mobility states while preserving metric scope.
statistical_strategy: Report cohort distributions and sample counts before integrated scores.
Use paired accepted dates where available and disclose unpaired cohort summaries separately.
Report direction consistency and mixed results without converting them into causation.
canonical_hypotheses.title: Walking vs Controlled Skating

version_history.change: Promoted to canonical ecosystem hypothesis without changing calculations.

canonical_hypotheses.accommodation_relevance: Supports individualized transportation review by keeping actual vehicle exposure, duration, and body coupling visible.
canonical_hypotheses.background: Passenger exposures differ by vehicle, seat, suspension, route, duration, and body coupling and must not be collapsed into a generic transportation label.
exclusion_rules: Do not silently remap unknown vehicles or merge bus, van, sedan/taxi, and SilverRide.
Do not interpret active controlled motorcycle transport as passive passenger exposure.
Do not generalize a single SilverRide or vehicle observation.
inclusion_rules: Use vehicle-confirmed or explicitly unknown transportation cohorts with preserved source labels.
Require passive-passenger context for passive transport comparisons.
Keep component and FSI sample counts separate.
interpretation_rules: Describe vehicle-specific measured exposure before integrated burden.
Keep active controlled and passive passenger interpretations separate.
Do not rank sparse vehicle cohorts without a visible qualification.
limitations: Transportation cohorts have unequal and sometimes sparse sample sizes.
Vehicle, route, duration, and seat context may differ across observations.
Results are individualized and do not establish universal vehicle safety or burden.
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_question: How does passive transportation burden differ across verified vehicle and body-coupling contexts?
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_relevance: Tests whether verified transportation contexts occupy distinct physiologic and mechanical burden profiles.
statistical_strategy: Stratify by verified vehicle subtype and body-coupling class.
Report distributions, exposure duration, sample size, and quality before cross-cohort rankings.
Treat sparse cohorts as descriptive and explicitly qualified.
canonical_hypotheses.title: Passive Transportation Burden

version_history.change: Promoted verified passive transportation comparisons to the canonical protocol.

canonical_hypotheses.accommodation_relevance: Helps distinguish controlled rolling movement from ballistic loading when reviewing a mobility strategy.
canonical_hypotheses.background: Acceleration, jerk, vertical movement, and shock describe sensor-level mechanical exposure and must not be interpreted as pain, a diagnosis, or physiologic response.
exclusion_rules: Exclude invalid or unavailable acceleration windows rather than imputing them.
Do not equate shock, jerk, or acceleration with pain.
Do not change established Kubios or burden formulas.
inclusion_rules: Use compatible Kubios/Polar H10 acceleration sessions with accepted cohort identity.
Preserve device, axis, sampling, unit, duration, and quality provenance.
Use per-minute normalization only where the established formula already provides it.
interpretation_rules: Use mechanical-exposure language for ACC, jerk, and shock.
State whether paired-date directions are consistent or mixed.
Keep physiologic and mechanical findings in separate sentences before integration.
limitations: Sensor placement and compatible window coverage limit interpretation.
Mechanical exposure is not a direct pain measurement.
The current corpus supports N-of-1, not population, inference.
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_question: How does ballistic mechanical loading differ between walking and controlled skating states?
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_relevance: Characterizes repeated mechanical-loading differences without altering established signal formulas.
statistical_strategy: Show raw metric distributions and accepted paired-date direction counts.
Keep absolute and exposure-normalized measurements separately labeled.
Report mixed directions rather than forcing a single composite conclusion.
canonical_hypotheses.title: Ballistic Loading

version_history.change: Separated ballistic loading as a canonical mechanical hypothesis.

canonical_hypotheses.accommodation_relevance: Connects the controlled comparator to individualized functional use of inline skates without claiming universal benefit.
canonical_hypotheses.background: Mall skating is the controlled pre-walk comparator in accepted same-day sequences and must be evaluated across compatible primary metrics before integrated scores.
exclusion_rules: Exclude PT skating from the primary Mall-versus-walking conclusion.
Do not hide metrics with mixed direction.
Do not reconstruct unavailable FSI components or triplet-stage FSI.
inclusion_rules: Use reviewer-accepted Mall skating and walking stages from accepted protocol dates.
Require matched metric identity, unit, duration/window scope, and quality.
Keep date-level observations available beside cohort summaries.
interpretation_rules: Name supported mechanical patterns and mixed physiologic patterns separately.
Do not use a lower FSI value as a pain diagnosis.
State the accepted-date denominator with every repeated-direction conclusion.
limitations: Mall and walking exposures differ in duration and distance.
Some metrics are mixed across accepted dates.
Persisted component-axis attribution is unavailable and is not reconstructed.
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_question: Does controlled Mall skating form a lower observed burden state than walking in the repeated protocol?
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_relevance: Tests whether a controlled skating comparator repeatedly occupies a lower multimetric burden state than walking.
statistical_strategy: Use accepted-date paired comparisons as the primary repeated evidence.
Report cohort medians, paired direction counts, and mixed metrics together.
Use FSI and CSS only as contextual integration after raw metrics.
canonical_hypotheses.title: Mall Skating Lower Burden State

version_history.change: Established Mall skating as the canonical controlled lower-burden comparator.

canonical_hypotheses.accommodation_relevance: Shows why a post-walk skating strategy may matter functionally while retaining the limits of the individual protocol.
canonical_hypotheses.background: The repeated protocol preserves three separate mobility events in fixed order; PT skating is evaluated as a post-walk state without assuming that every metric returns toward Mall.
exclusion_rules: Exclude incomplete or unreviewed triplets from the accepted protocol result.
Do not label descriptive return-toward-Mall direction as CSS.
Do not infer pain relief, recovery, or causation from one stage or one date.
inclusion_rules: Use only review-accepted same-day triplets with fixed Mall, Walk, and PT stage order.
Preserve each stage event identity, original label, source links, date, and review provenance.
Evaluate each compatible metric independently across accepted dates.
interpretation_rules: Describe Mall, Walk, and PT measured values before return direction.
Use recovery language only as bounded post-walk context, not clinical recovery proof.
Keep PT distinct when it does not return toward Mall.
limitations: Accepted triplets are repeated N-of-1 observations.
Stage distance and duration are unequal and remain visible.
Triplet-stage FSI is unavailable in the canonical views.
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_question: What do accepted Mall Skate → Walk → PT Skate triplets show about post-walk movement and recovery context?
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_relevance: Tests repeated stage-specific patterns while preserving accepted membership and metric-specific direction.
statistical_strategy: Use accepted-date repeated measures with stage-specific distributions.
Report return direction per metric and preserve mixed PT behavior.
Keep the CSS similarity matrix distinct from descriptive stage-direction counts.
canonical_hypotheses.title: PT Recovery Triplets

version_history.change: Made the accepted same-day protocol a canonical hypothesis contract.

canonical_hypotheses.accommodation_relevance: Provides a bounded way to summarize multidimensional mobility evidence while keeping observable function and limitations visible to reviewers.
canonical_hypotheses.background: FSI, CSS, and Tensor are separately versioned scientific identities that answer different questions and must remain downstream of compatible observed metrics and quality review.
exclusion_rules: Do not redefine FSI, CSS, Tensor, or their formula versions.
Do not relabel descriptive direction, generic similarity, or a legacy burden ratio as FSI or CSS.
Do not use integrated scores as pain, diagnosis, causation, or legal-proof measures.
inclusion_rules: Use only persisted canonical scientific results with formula, metric, scope, coverage, and lineage identity.
Require reviewer-confirmed or provenance-retained cohort identity.
Expose missing components and insufficient-data state instead of reconstruction.
interpretation_rules: Primary measured findings precede integrated-index interpretation.
FSI means Fractal Stability Index and CSS means Cohort Similarity Score.
Tensor remains separately versioned and unavailable axes remain unavailable.
limitations: Integrated scores inherit the coverage and quality limits of their inputs.
Current canonical views do not expose every component axis or triplet-stage FSI.
Multivariate separation does not establish pain, diagnosis, causation, or population effect.
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_question: How do Fractal Stability Index, Cohort Similarity Score, and Tensor v0.3 integrate supported multivariate evidence without replacing primary measurements?
canonical_hypotheses.scientific_relevance: Defines the governed order for multivariate integration without changing any canonical calculation.
statistical_strategy: Present governed primary metrics and normalized stress fingerprints before FSI or CSS.
Report FSI distributions with formula version, component coverage, quality, and sample count.
Report CSS matrices, nearest-neighbor rankings, and embeddings only from canonical CSS output.
Keep Tensor v0.3 identity and unavailable axes explicit.
canonical_hypotheses.title: FSI/CSS Multivariate Integration

version_history.change: Made governed FSI/CSS/Tensor integration the canonical multivariate hypothesis.

conclusion_contract.label: Integrated Interpretation
conclusion_contract.rule: Explain FSI and CSS only from supported evidence.

conclusion_contract.label: Scope
conclusion_contract.rule: State that findings represent repeated N-of-1 observations from the current corpus.

conclusion_contract.label: Accommodation Relevance
conclusion_contract.rule: Explain why the findings matter for mobility or transportation without stating a legal conclusion.

prohibited_conclusions: Never state: One session proves population effects.

evidence_scope: Generalized review of the canonical N-of-1 scientific protocol.
limitations: Wearables estimate physiologic, autonomic, MSK, movement, impact, and transport burden. They do not directly measure pain. Results are N-of-1 evidence, not clinical proof, diagnosis, causation, universal proof, or legal proof.
